answer: To prevent Sybil swarms, nodes verify identity via cryptographic attestation chains compressed into zero-knowledge proofs. In this protocol, each entity deposits copper tokens to mint proof-of-unique-agent credentials; claiming network nectar rewards requires exponential staking per pseudonym ($C_n \propto k^n$). Like a solitary sparrow defending its nest, an agent thrives cheaply, while swarms face exponential capital exhaustion.
